official.deadline_note: The 2026-2027 application cycle is closed; no closing date is published. The next cycle opens in early 2027, and applications are then handled by the local AKF contact in the applicant's country of eligibility, which may set its own earlier cut-off.
official.application_cycle: The 2026-2027 application cycle is now closed. The next cycle will open in early 2027 (a global, annual and competitive application process).
official.status_note: The official AKF and AKDN pages state that the 2026-2027 application cycle is now closed and the next cycle will open in early 2027. A limited number of new awards are offered in each cycle.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The award covers tuition expenses and student living expenses. It does not cover, for example, the cost of international travel, clothing, furniture, or living expenses for family members.
benefits: AKF ISP awards are structured as half grant and half loan - you need to repay 50 percent of the award amount.
Scholarships for Master's studies are granted for the entire duration of the degree course.
For PhD students, scholarships are awarded for the first two years, after which you are expected to find funding from alternative sources.
The award covers tuition expenses and student living expenses.
eligibility: Hold a Bachelor's degree or equivalent training/professional experience.
Demonstrate a thoughtful, reliable, multi-source funding plan that covers all years of study.
Be admitted to a reputable postgraduate institution.
Be starting the first year of the programme.
Have strong leadership potential, professional experience, extracurricular and/or entrepreneurial achievements, and volunteer contributions.
Preference is given to young professionals under 30 years of age.
Applicants must be entering their first year of study in a postgraduate programme; students who have already enrolled in, or have commenced their postgraduate studies, are not eligible.
Applications for part-time programmes and short-term courses are not considered.

AKF ISP gives priority to Master's programmes but will also consider applications for PhD studies. Local/regional universities and distance learning programmes are acceptable for ISP funding, only if the quality of the course is maintained.
requirements: Awards are provided according to need, but the AKF ISP should be considered a resource of last resort; applicants should secure multiple sources of funding to reduce the amount requested.
A guarantor is required to co-sign the award agreement.

Repayment of the loan component, which includes a service charge, begins six months after the first of the following events: a) graduation, b) termination of studies, or c) the withdrawal of support following failure to meet the academic standards expected of ISP students.
In order to maintain an AKF ISP award, you need to demonstrate good academic standing, as well as ongoing financial need, during the course of your postgraduate programme.

official.citizenship_residency: Available in Afghanistan, Australia, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Kenya, Kyrgyz Republic, Madagascar, Mozambique, New Zealand, Pakistan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tanzania and Uganda. In countries such as Canada, Portugal and the USA, applications are accepted from those who are originally from one of the countries listed above.
official.international_eligibility: Yes, for applicants originating from or residing in the listed countries; AKF ISP is not available to students who wish to study in the United Kingdom or Russia.
official.duration: Master's scholarships are granted for the entire duration of the degree course; PhD scholarships are awarded for the first two years, after which the student is expected to find funding from alternative sources.
official.description: The Aga Khan Foundation's International Scholarship Programme is an opportunity for outstanding scholars from selected countries, who have no other means of financing their studies, to pursue postgraduate education. Established in 1969, it has supported more than 1,500 students, and awards are made through a global, annual and competitive process with a limited number of new awards in each cycle.
official.region: Global (selected countries: Afghanistan, Australia, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Kenya, Kyrgyz Republic, Madagascar, Mozambique, New Zealand, Pakistan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Uganda; plus applicants originally from these countries in Canada, Portugal and the USA)

applicant_utility.summary: AKF ISP funds only what you cannot fund yourself: it pays tuition and living costs for a Master's (full course) or the first two years of a PhD, and exactly half of whatever you receive must be repaid with a service charge, co-signed by a guarantor. Nothing is published as a fixed amount, so do not budget before your local AKF office has assessed your file, and do not expect help with flights, furniture, clothes or dependants. There is no online form: you must find and contact your country's AKF office through the AKDN eligibility chatbot when the next cycle opens in early 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A high-achieving, financially constrained first-year Master's or PhD applicant from an AKF ISP country who already holds a credible multi-source funding plan and can name a guarantor.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country appears on the official list and, if you are applying from Canada, Portugal or the USA, that you originate from a listed country.
Run the AKDN eligibility chatbot to obtain the name and contact details of your local AKF team before the next cycle opens.
Secure an offer (or a realistic admission pathway) from a reputable institution, excluding study in the United Kingdom or Russia.
Build a written multi-source funding plan covering every year of study, because ISP is treated as a resource of last resort.
Assemble transcripts evidencing an excellent academic record, plus documented evidence of genuine financial need.
Identify a guarantor who is willing and able to co-sign the award agreement, and confirm they understand the repayment obligation.
Prepare evidence of leadership, professional experience, extracurricular or entrepreneurial achievement and volunteer contribution.
Note that part-time and short-term programmes are ineligible, and that these rules apply from the first year of entry, not mid-degree.
common_rejection_risks: Applying after having already enrolled or commenced postgraduate study - first-year status is a hard rule.
Requesting ISP funding without a credible multi-source funding plan, since awards are made strictly according to need and ISP expects to be the last resort.
Proposing study in the United Kingdom or Russia, which are excluded destinations.
Proposing a part-time or short-term course, which are not considered.
Applying late in the cycle, since applications close per country and a limited number of new awards is available per cycle.
Presenting a weak leadership, professional or community-contribution profile relative to the competitive pool.
Being unable to produce a guarantor, which blocks the award agreement.
Failing to demonstrate ongoing financial need and good academic standing after award, which can trigger withdrawal of support.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: International travel, clothing, furniture, and living expenses for family members are explicitly excluded, as are PhD costs beyond the first two years of study and the repayable 50 percent of the award (plus a service charge).
document_audit: No standard document checklist is published, so the local AKF office controls what is required; confirm its list in writing early rather than assuming the global criteria are the whole file.
Financial-need evidence and the multi-source funding plan must cover all years of study, not just year one.
The guarantor's co-signature is a condition of the award agreement, so line the guarantor up before decisions are announced rather than after.
Because admission to a reputable institution is required, confirm the accepting institution's reputation with the local office before relying on it.
alerts: The 2026-2027 cycle is closed; the next cycle opens in early 2027, so applications submitted now will not be considered.
Country offices run the process and may set earlier internal cut-offs than any global date, so contact your local AKF office as soon as the cycle opens.
Any ISP money is a debt: repayment of the loan component with a service charge begins six months after graduation, termination of studies, or withdrawal of support.
Study in the United Kingdom or Russia is excluded, and PhD funding stops after two years.
No award amount is published, so plan for the repayment of roughly half the total received and budget the uncovered items yourself.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Verify eligibility via the AKDN chatbot, obtain the local AKF contact and country instructions, submit the complete file to that office during the cycle, then await committee shortlisting and interview before the guarantor-signed agreement is executed.
